symbols.name: _ac35_violations
symbols.doc: The porcelain lines AC-35 (as re-scoped) fails on: a status entry for one of the seven vendored files, or any __pycache__ entry. Everything else in the checkout — including its owner's own uncommitted work — is none of this ticket's business.

symbols.name: test_ac35_rescoped_check_still_fails_on_a_vendored_modification
symbols.doc: AC-35's re-scope must NOT be a tautology. Each of the seven vendored files, reported modified/deleted/renamed, still fails the check — and a __pycache__ entry does too — proven against the pure check function, without a byte written into the read-only checkouts.

symbols.name: test_ac35_rescoped_check_ignores_the_owners_own_work
symbols.doc: The other half of the q3 ruling: the exact status lines that were failing the suite — Evan's own 2026-08-13 edits, in files this ticket never reads — are NOT violations.

symbols.name: test_ac35_wired_test_fires_end_to_end
symbols.doc: The proof one level up: the WIRED test (not just the helper) fails when the status reader reports a modified vendored file. The reader is monkeypatched to simulate the signal, so nothing touches the read-only checkout; skips loudly when no checkout is present, exactly like the test it is proving.

symbols.name: test_ac39a_tree_dependent_checks_skip_loudly_when_absent
symbols.doc: AC-39(a), exercised directly: with AUTOSQL_GIMS_TREE and AUTOSQL_GUTS_TREE pointed at paths that do not exist, the tree-dependent checks in *this* module report SKIPPED and name the path.

symbols.name: test_ac39b_manifest_halves_never_skip
symbols.doc: AC-39(b): re-assert that every manifest-half / spike-file check is unconditional — no `pytest.skip` anywhere in its path — by re-running the underlying comparison directly rather than through pytest, so this test cannot itself be skipped into a false pass.

symbols.name: _files_up_can_execute
symbols.doc: Everything `./run-demo up` and a pick can run: the launcher itself and every Python file in the demo tree OUTSIDE demo/tests/ (the tests are exactly where the tree variables are ALLOWED — that is AC-34/AC-35's loud-skip machinery). demo/.venv is installed third-party code and demo/frontend is `build-ui`'s Node toolchain; neither is the demo's own `up` path.

symbols.name: test_ac39c_nothing_up_runs_can_even_name_a_tree
symbols.doc: AC-39(c), the standing static half: no file `up` or a pick executes mentions the tree variables or the checkout paths AT ALL, so `./run-demo up`, the seed, the builder and the server cannot depend on a GIMS checkout on any machine — there is no code through which they could.
